## CHAPTER XXX.

### On the Reign of the Sun.

Now you approach the end of your work, and you have almost completed your task; now everything looks like pure gold <term>auri obryzi</term> <gloss>refined gold</gloss>, and the <term>lac virginis</term> <gloss>virgin's milk</gloss> <note>In alchemy, this term often refers to a white, mercurial liquid or solvent used to nourish the matter.</note>, with which you soak this matter, becomes very yellow <term>citrinescit</term> <gloss>turns the color of a citron</gloss>. Now render immortal thanks to God, the giver of all good things, who has brought the work this far. Pray to Him as a suppliant, that He may guide your counsel from now on, so that you do not happen to lose the work entirely by attempting to rush it when it is almost finished. Consider now that you have waited for almost seven months, and it would not be sane to destroy everything in a single little hour. Therefore, be extremely cautious, and all the more so as you are closer to perfection. 

If you proceed cautiously, these noteworthy things will occur to you: first, you will observe a certain yellow sweat on the body, and finally yellow vapors—while the body settles—tinged with violet, and sometimes with a dark purple. <summary>This page describes the final transition into the Reign of the Sun, where the alchemical matter turns a distinct lemon-yellow color. The author provides a strong warning to the practitioner to remain patient and cautious during these final stages to avoid ruining months of labor.</summary>
